content: Migrant and seasonal agricultural workers face significant obstacles in accessing healthcare services. Frequent migration disrupts continuity of care, making it difficult for these individuals to establish long-term relationships with healthcare providers. Language barriers further complicate communication with medical professionals, limiting their ability to understand and follow medical advice. Additionally, their limited and often unpredictable work hours reduce the time available to seek medical attention. Many of these workers are also unfamiliar with the healthcare resources available to them, which prevents them from utilizing necessary services. These challenges collectively increase the likelihood of delayed diagnosis and management of diabetes, leading to a higher risk of severe complications that are both life-threatening and costly. To address these issues, innovative care delivery models, such as mobile healthcare units and telehealth services, can be implemented. These approaches bring medical care directly to migrant farmworkers, overcoming logistical and accessibility barriers while improving health outcomes.
